glosses: to annihilate, to destroy, to eradicate, to exterminate (to reduce to nothing)
полностью уничтожать
To damage beyond use or repair; to damage (something) to the point that it effectively ceases to exist.

examples.text: The earthquake destroyed several apartment complexes.
Hooligans destroy unprovoked.
Iesus answered, and said vnto them, Destroy this temple, and in three dayes I will raise it vp.

Repeated use of this type of [water] on plants results in deflocculation[] of the soil. Good quality soil consists of loose aggregates which provide natural aeration and ease of root run. Sodium accumulation in soil destroys this natural flocculation and causes the soil to pack.
Krav is a martial art of last resort that assumes no quarter and focuses purely on disarming, disabling and, if necessary, destroying your opponent.

glosses: To neutralize, undo a property or condition.

examples.text: Smoking destroys the natural subtlety of the palate.

glosses: To put down or euthanize.

examples.text: Destroying a rabid dog is required by law.

glosses: To severely disrupt the well-being of (a person); ruin.

examples.text: Her divorce destroyed her; she had a nervous breakdown and was severely depressed for more than a year.
Other girls in the foster home are eager to destroy her and get her kicked out of the place. It's a tough situation.

glosses: To utterly defeat; to crush.

examples.text: Remember when Germany destroyed Brazil 7–1 in the World Cup?
Growing up, [Kevin] Durant told me, he was a sore loser. That all changed one day when he was 11, after he got destroyed by his father in a game of one on one in the driveway.

glosses: To remove data.

examples.text: The memory leak happened because we forgot to destroy the temporary lists.

glosses: To exhaust completely and thus recreate or build up.

examples.text: This exercise is going to destroy all parts of your shoulders.

glosses: To penetrate sexually in an aggressive way.

examples.text: She got destroyed by her lover on the carpet.

glosses: To sing a song extremely poorly.

examples.text: JAMES CARTER: The man's destroying a classic!

glosses: To eat food quickly, hungrily or completely.

examples.text: I could destroy some wings right now.

glosses: To kill or otherwise permanently eliminate all of (a population of pests or undesirables), usually intentionally.

examples.text: We'll use poison to exterminate the rats.

The geth are a humanoid race of networked A.I.s. They were created by the quarians 300 years ago as tools of labor and war. When the geth showed signs of self-evolution, the quarians attempted to exterminate them. The geth won the resulting war. This example has led to legal, systematic repression of artificial intelligences in galactic society.

Somewhat unsurprisingly, unleashing the most powerful navy on the planet with carte blanche to exterminate slavers on sight saw a dramatic and sudden collapse in slaver numbers in the late 1840s and early 1850s.

glosses: To bring a definite end to; to finish completely.

examples.text: The public school failed to exterminate truancy.

glosses: To use up.

examples.text: The power plant consumes 30 tons of coal per hour.

glosses: To eat.

examples.text: Baby birds consume their own weight in food each day.

Concerns were raised around the ability of Milky Way species to consume proteins from Andromeda, so seed banks formed a significant part of the arks' cargo. We now know it is safe to consume food grown or hunted here, though enzyme supplements are recommended and have become a social norm at mealtimes.

glosses: To completely occupy the thoughts or attention of.

examples.text: Desire consumed him.

glosses: To destroy completely.

examples.text: The building was consumed by fire.
If he were putting to my house the brand / That shall consume it.

Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth consume, and where thieves do not break through to steal: […]

glosses: To waste away slowly.

examples.text: Therefore, let Benedick, like cover'd fire, / Consume away in sighs.
But, sir, you see how weak I am. You must see that I have been consuming from day to day […].
He assured her the child was consuming at that moment in the next room.

glosses: To trade money for good or services as an individual.

examples.text: In a materialistic society, individuals are taught to consume, consume, consume.
If you consume this product while in Japan, you may be subject to consumption tax.

glosses: To absorb information, especially through the mass media.

examples.text: The Internet has changed the way we consume news.

glosses: 殲滅，消滅
